question: Does changing the quantum stress of the independently heralded Wilson-Maxwell field change the vacuum-calibrated weak optical propagation law of that same box?
source: Existing four oriented charged Wilson circuits at z=0, winding +1, pointer 0 followed by a total-number-one filter; fresh vacuum control.
ports: Oriented individual face Wilson loops in xy, xz, yz planes with base (side/2, side/2, 0); receiver parallel with base z=1 or side-1. Measure signed susceptibility between the loops.
weak_limit: Evaluate the zero-amplitude Wilson kick commutator separately in each state. Test finite kicks on adjacent xz faces at t=side/2 for every box.
clock_control: Increase all free propagation frequencies by 20% at fixed states and quadrature coefficients. This changes the law as a detector control only.
records: Independent ensembles for counter, electric/magnetic squared quadratures, and signed receiver. Multinomially sample exact capped probabilities, stored as sufficient statistics.
criteria: Verify spectral energy equals the sum of three integrated Maxwell stress components at every tested time (closure 1e-10); field-square records resolve positive stress trace above five standard errors. Report exact weak-limit discrepancy and finite-pulse sampling errors. A changed-clock control must differ in at least one registered channel. Interpret equivalence only for this box's retarded optical readout.
